title: SecurityEvent
description: Normalized security event. This is the ONLY shape that crosses trust boundary TB-2 (log ingestion). Every field originating from outside the system (user_id, source_ip, device_id, resource, metadata.*) MUST be treated as untrusted, attacker-controllable data by every downstream consumer.

event_id.description: Unique event identifier, assigned at ingestion (not by the source). Used for deduplication (C-10).

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 with millisecond precision, UTC. e.g. 2026-03-12T09:41:02.150Z. Full precision is kept in the data layer; the frontend may round for display.

ingested_at.description: Server-assigned ingestion time, distinct from the (untrusted) source-reported timestamp. Used to catch impossible/future timestamps (Phase 6).

user_id.description: Stable internal identifier, not a raw username string. UNTRUSTED — may be null for pre-auth events (e.g. failed login with unknown account).

attempted_username.description: Raw username string as submitted at login. UNTRUSTED FREE TEXT — the primary prompt-injection vector (T-06). Never interpolate this into an LLM prompt without delimiting/escaping (C-02). Length-capped at ingestion.

source_ip.description: UNTRUSTED. Validated as a syntactically well-formed IPv4/IPv6 address at ingestion; content beyond that is not trusted.

resource.description: Resource or endpoint accessed, e.g. 'srv-grades-db'. UNTRUSTED FREE TEXT in principle; constrain to a known resource enum where possible.

severity.description: Assigned by the ingestion/detection layer, never trusted verbatim from the source.

metadata.description: Free-form additional context (user-agent, role_before/role_after, etc). UNTRUSTED. Capped in total size (C-01) and never passed to an LLM without sanitization (C-02, C-12). Must not contain raw credentials or full PII (C-12).
